tasks.short: Take requests and agree dates, hold preparation meetings, collect details for the register and write the ceremony text with the family.

steps.what: Families request a baptism or wedding through the website form, pick a free date and give their details; by phone today
Minister takes requests for baptisms and weddings by phone and agrees dates
Minister prepares people for participation in religious ceremonies in meetings
Minister collects the personal details for the ceremony and the member register from the form
Minister checks the register entry: names, dates, the ceremony and the family's agreement to registration
Minister posts the checked entry to the member register
Minister writes the ceremony text with the family

tasks.design: Families request a ceremony through a form on the congregation's website ({CMS}) that shows free dates from the church calendar and collects the details needed, including whether they agree to registration. The minister confirms the date and checks the details before they go into the member register. Preparation meetings and writing the ceremony text stay with the minister.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates were agreed by phone and details written down by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Website forms can show free dates and collect details with consent questions.
tasks.still_hard: Families often want to talk first; the form does not replace that call.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a couple say what their vows mean to them.

reach.learn: Whether form details cut register errors.

evidence.claim: Online request forms can show free dates from a calendar and collect details.
Since 2020 the Protestant Church registers a new person in LRP only after checking they know of the registration and do not object to SILA updates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the request to the ceremony text; the ceremony itself is outside.
Input contract: church calendar kept by the church administrator; register fields set by the denomination; fallback is phone and paper.
Preparation and writing do not change.
Families' time is shown in s5 as customer time and is not counted again as new work. s1 keeps 40 for confirming dates and talking with families who prefer to phone.
research_questions: Are register details complete more often?

incremental.description: No new work: calls with families who prefer to talk first are inside s1's remaining time, and families' form time is shown in s5.

approvals.approved_version: The register entry with names, dates and ceremony exactly as checked by the minister in s3b, with the family's agreement to registration, posted once to the member register; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many families keep phoning and give details on paper, so s1 and s3 keep 70 (9.3); high: requests through the form as designed (18.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Learn who needs a visit, arrange visits, visit people at home, in hospital or prison, and note visits made.

steps.what: Pastoral team members enter visit signals in the shared confidential list
Minister learns who needs a visit from members, chaplains and the pastoral team
Minister phones to arrange the visit
Minister visits people in homes, hospitals or prisons to provide comfort and support
Minister notes visits made with the date and a short note; in a notebook today

tasks.design: A confidential visit list shared only with the pastoral team ({OTHER}) collects who needs a visit, so fewer calls are needed to find out, and the minister notes visits there with a date and a short note, never health details; this first record keeps its time. Arranging and making visits stay with the minister.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visit needs came by phone and word of mouth; visits were noted in a private notebook.
tasks.enabler_now: Small shared lists with strict access are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: The most important signals still come in conversation after a service.
tasks.human_edge: Sitting quietly with someone who has just lost a partner.

reach.learn: Whether a shared list avoids missed or double visits.

evidence.claim: Shared lists with access for named people only are simple to set up.
Church membership reveals religious belief; it may not be disclosed outside the church body without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from visit signals to the visit log; follow-up care is outside.
Input contract: visit signals entered by the pastoral team; fallback is phone and notebook.
Arranging, visiting and noting visits do not change. The pastoral team's entries (s0) replace phone calls and are outside the minister's savings.

incremental.description: No new work: reading the shared list is s1.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the team rarely enters signals, so the minister still phones round and s1 keeps 85 (2.1); high: signals entered as designed (5.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare training sessions, train leaders of youth and community groups, coach them and record completed training.

steps.what: Minister prepares training sessions for group leaders
Minister trains leaders of church, community or youth groups
Minister records who attended each training session
Minister coaches leaders one to one
Minister tracks completed training and certificates in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: A shared library of training modules in the denomination's document space ({DOCS}) gives a starting point for sessions, and attendance recorded at each session builds the training record per leader with the date and validity of certificates. Training and coaching stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sessions were built from scratch and records kept in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared module libraries and simple attendance records are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Good leaders grow through coaching, not modules.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which young leader is ready for more responsibility.

reach.learn: Whether shared modules raise training quality.

evidence.claim: Shared module libraries and attendance-based training records are simple to set up.
Records of volunteers' certificates are personal data; keep only date and validity.

assumptions: Boundary: from leader needs to training records; appointing leaders is outside.
Input contract: module library kept by the denomination's training office; fallback is building sessions from scratch.
Training and coaching do not change.
Leaders' time is outside the minister's savings.

incremental.description: No new work: recording attendance is shown as step s2b.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: library modules rarely fit the groups, so sessions are built mostly from scratch and s1 keeps 90 (11.5); high: modules as designed (16.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the season programme, prepare session materials, lead sessions, register participants and remind them before sessions.

steps.what: Minister plans the religious education program for the season
Minister prepares discussion questions and activities for each session

loop.input: The texts chosen for the session, the session's aims from the denomination's curriculum and the group's age band; no participant data.
loop.output: Draft discussion questions, activities and a short explanation.
loop.check: Code checks every quoted passage matches the licensed edition word for word and every aim has an activity. The minister checks that each question and activity serves its aim and reads the passage fairly, and edits every draft.
loop.stop: One draft per session; on failure the minister prepares by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Activities for a specific group and text need free text; a fixed workbook does not fit every group.

steps.what: Minister leads the education sessions
Participants sign up for the programme in the website form; by e-mail today
Minister keeps and confirms the participant list
Minister checks the reminder before it goes: session date, place, text and the participant list
Minister releases the checked reminder, which goes to the participants before the session

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts discussion questions and activities from the chosen texts and the curriculum aims for the group's age, checked against the licensed text, and the minister edits each draft. Participants register through a website form ({CMS}); once the minister confirms the list each week, reminders go out before each session. Planning the season and leading sessions stay with the minister.
tasks.previous_blocker: Session materials were prepared from scratch and registrations kept from e-mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can draft questions and activities from given texts; registration forms send reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Faith formation depends on trust in the group; materials are a small part.
tasks.human_edge: Answering a teenager's hard question honestly.
tasks.altitude: The minister edits drafted session materials instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether drafted materials help volunteers prepare.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft discussion questions and activities from given texts.
Congregational education is not an Annex III area; AI literacy duties apply to any AI use.

assumptions: Boundary: from the season plan to sessions held; pastoral care for participants is outside.
Input contract: curriculum aims from the denomination; licensed edition of the texts bought by the congregation; fallback is preparing by hand.

Planning and leading do not change. s2 keeps 70 because the minister still shapes each session; the draft gives questions and activities to edit. Participants' sign-up time is shown in s6 and not counted again. s5 keeps 20 for the release.
No participant data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of each draft does the minister keep?

already_counted.description: Minister confirms the participant list each week.

incremental.description: Minister sets up the registration form each season.

approvals.approved_version: The reminder with session date, place and text exactly as checked by the minister in s4b, sent once to the participants on the checked list; a changed text, date or list needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts are mostly rewritten and many participants keep e-mailing, so s2 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 60 (12.2); high: drafts and form as designed (19.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The minister keeps ceremonies, visits, training and teaching; requests, lists and first drafts of session materials shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A minister who spends saved hours with people rather than lists.
